The combination of amiodarone and droperidol is contraindicated as both drugs increase the QTc interval. 3. The combination of amisulpride and droperidol is contraindicated due to an increased risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 4. Droperidol should not be co-administered with disopyramide, ibutilide, indapamide, pentamidine, pimozide, procainamide, quinidine, or sotalol, as all these drugs increase the QTc interval. 5. Adagrasib and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 6. Alfuzosin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Alternate drugs should be considered. 7. Amitriptyline, amoxapine, and anagrelide, when combined with droperidol, increase the QTc interval. Alternate therapies are recommended. 8. Droperidol reduces the effects of apomorphine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval, and their combination should be avoided. 9. Aripiprazole and droperidol both increase the QTc interval and sedation. Use with caution and monitor closely. 10. Arsenic trioxide, artemether, and artemether/lumefantrine, when combined with droperidol, increase the QTc interval. Alternate drugs are recommended. 11. Asenapine (oral or transdermal) and droperidol both increase the QTc interval and sedation. Use alternate drugs or monitor closely. 12. Atomoxetine and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternate drugs. 13. Benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen and droperidol increase sedation. Limit use to patients without alternative treatment options. 14. Bromocriptine’s effects are reduced by droperidol due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination. 15. Buprenorphine (subdermal, transdermal, or long-acting injection) and droperidol increase sedation. Limit use to patients without alternative options. 16. Cabergoline’s effects are reduced by droperidol due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Droperidol and sodium oxybates increase sedation and respiratory depression, potentially leading to coma or death. Use only when no alternatives exist, and monitor closely. 18. Ceritinib, chlorpromazine, clarithromycin, clomipramine, and clozapine, when combined with droperidol, increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 19. Degarelix, desflurane, desipramine, and dofetilide, when combined with droperidol, increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 20. Donepezil and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 21. Dopamine’s effects are reduced by droperidol due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Doxepin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 23. Dronedarone and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 24. Efavirenz, eliglustat, and encorafenib, when combined with droperidol, increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 25. Droperidol and entrectinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 26. Epinephrine (including racemic) and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 27. Eribulin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. If co-administration is necessary, monitor ECG closely. 28. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate) and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 29. Escitalopram increases droperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 30. Fentanyl (all forms) and droperidol increase sedation. Limit use to patients without alternative options. 31. Fexinidazole and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 32. Fingolimod and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 33. Fluconazole and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 34. Fluphenazine and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 35. Droperidol and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 36. Gemifloxacin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 37. Gilteritinib and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 38. Droperidol and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. If unavoidable, monitor ECG and withhold if QTc exceeds 500 ms or changes by more than 60 ms from baseline. 39. Droperidol and glasdegib both increase the QTc interval. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. 40. Granisetron and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 41. Droperidol and haloperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 43. Hydroxyzine increases droperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 44. Imipramine and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 45. Inotuzumab and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. If unavoidable, monitor ECG and electrolytes before and after initiation. 46. Isoflurane and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 47. Itraconazole and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 48. Ivosidenib and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or monitor for QTc prolongation. 49. Droperidol and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 50. Lefamulin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 51. Droperidol reduces the effects of levodopa (oral or inhaled) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration. 52. Droperidol and levoketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 53. Droperidol reduces the effects of lisuride due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 54. Lithium and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 55. Lofepramine and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 56. Droperidol and lumefantrine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 57. Macimorelin and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration with QT-prolonging drugs. 58. Maprotiline and droperidol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternate drugs. 59. Methohexital and droperidol both increase sedation. Limit use to patients without alternative options. 60. Droperidol reduces the effects of methyldopa due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. This list continues with similar patterns of interactions, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, or avoidance of combinations that increase QTc intervals, sedation, or other toxicities.
